title: GSM5591871
treatment_protocol_ch1: stage of menstrual cycle: window of implantation
molecule_ch1: Endometrial gland isolation was performed by enzyme digestion within 1 h of tissue collection. Endometrial tissue pieces were digested with 0.7 mg/ml type 1A collagenase in 50:50 DMEM/ Ham’s F12 nutrient mixture, containing 5% streptomycin at 37°C for 2 x 15 min intervals with gentle agitation. The endometrial gland fraction was purified and passed through a 50 µm sieve to remove other endometrial cell types. Endometrial glands were then stored in QIAol lysis reagent at -80°C until RNA extraction
taxid_ch1: Library preparation was performed using the TruSeq® Stranded mRNA Library Prep kit (Illumina). The final library was quantified by a Roche KAPA library quantification kit (Illumina) and by the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyser.
data_processing.1: Gene expression analysis: Raw FASTQ reads were aligned to the human genome via STAR 2.7.3a alignment using human genome 38 and trimmed with trimmomatic. QC was assessed by FastQC (version 0.11.3). Gene count data were normalised, and differential gene expression analysis was carried out in RStudio R-4.0.3 package DESeq2 (version 1.30.1).
data_processing.2: Splicing and gene transcript expression analysis: Raw FASTQ reads were trimmed for the adapter sequence and quality filtering (reads containing N > 10%, reads where >50% of read has Qscore<= 5). Paired FASTQ files were aligned to GRCh38 human genome reference using GENCODE v29 gene annotations and  STAR v2.6.0a splice aware aligner, using ENCODE recommend options. The two-pass alignment method was used, with soft clipping activated. BAM files sorted by chromosomal coordinates were assessed for saturation of known splice junctions were calculated using RSeqQC v3.0.1. Salmon tool was used to perform transcript abundance estimates from raw FASTQ files using selective alignment with a decoy-aware transcriptome built from GRCh38. rMATs v4.0.2 (rMATS turbo ) was used to statistically measure differences in splicing between replicates of wild-type and mutant sequence. BAM files aligned with STAR v2.6.0a two-pass method with soft clipping suppressed were used as input.
